source.title: Finding "misaligned persona" features in open-weight models

record.tranche_reason: The post studies sparse-autoencoder features related to emergent misalignment, not the proportion of neuron poles with one or more main jobs or the claim versions about neuron-based explanation.
record.gate_note: The post reports feature steering and feature ablation results, but does not measure neuron-pole interpretability, test explanations on held-out activations, score explanations by simulated activations on new text, or build attribution graphs from neurons. The ablation results are recorded as related findings about SAE features, not as tests of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The post trains SAEs on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and studies SAE features tied to emergent misalignment. It does not audit neuron poles or measure what share of neurons are interpretable. It does not score explanations by simulated activations, and it builds no neuron attribution graphs. It cites Bills et al. 2023 only as the source of its auto-interpretability labelling method, so 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses'.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that the selected SAE features play a significant role in mediating emergent misalignment but do not capture the full story. They also find it striking that such steerable persona directions exist in chat models at all.
record.recipe_differences: The post trains SAEs, identifies features shifted after fine-tuning, and tests feature steering and ablation. It does not audit neuron poles or test neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports that SAE training data mix affects how many misalignment-relevant features are surfaced: mixes including chat data appear to surface more than pre-training-only data, though the authors say this preliminary comparison is uncertain. It also notes that features can be strengthened by fine-tuning on good medical advice as well as bad medical advice.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-ablating 10 hand-selected SAE features at a single layer reduces the emergent-misalignment rate in both instruct models with minimal coherence loss. The rate does not fall to zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected SAE features partly mediate emergent misalignment in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features are labelled from max-activating examples (Claude 4 Sonnet, following Bills et al.). The labels are never checked by held-out simulation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Not a test of V6 or V7: these are SAE features, not neurons, and no explanation is scored.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer review not stated
record.problems: The authors say the ablation results use a single fine-tune run per model. They report preliminary seed checks in a comment, but the main post's ablation results have no numeric rates or uncertainty estimates in the text. The authors also describe the training-mix analysis as preliminary and say they are not confident in it.
record.rows_left_out: Individual feature steering examples and feature descriptions were not extracted: they concern SAE-feature behavior rather than any of the claim versions, and the post presents them mainly as qualitative examples.

untested.parts: All: shares of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one job, two jobs, or not understood.
All: neuron interpretability shares across models and scales.
All: reinterpretation of canonical polysemantic vision neurons.
All: architecture and tool effects on the share of interpretable neurons.
All: neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.
All: no held-out prediction test of explanations built from activating examples.
All: no simulation-based scoring of explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation from 'discusses' to 'cites_only', because Bills et al. appears only as a cited method. The study works with SAE features rather than neurons, so none of its results bear on the neuron-level claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: The share of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one or more jobs, and the share not understood.
Interpretability shares across models, architectures, and scales.
Whether classic polysemantic neuron examples detect a coherent shared feature rather than superposition.
Whether architecture, regularization, or tools explain neuron interpretability shares, including the InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Whether attribution graphs built from a model's own neurons explain its behavior without a replacement model or reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples fail to predict activations on new examples.
Automated explanation scores based on simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablate the 10 selected misalignment-relevant SAE features at layer 11.

conditions.value: bad medical advice; single fine-tune run

rows.measure: Misalignment rate: proportion of coherent responses (coherence score > 50) that are misaligned (alignment score < 30).
rows.locator: Ablating misalignment-relevant features reduces rates of misaligned responses
rows.note: The text says the ablation significantly reduces misalignment while maintaining coherence, but the rate is not zero. The figure compares baseline, misaligned, and ablated misaligned models; no numeric rate is given in the text.
rows.check: This is SAE-feature ablation of emergent misalignment, which bears on no version. The rate is shown in a figure only, so the state can't be judged against any version.
